item.title: Houthi strike hits Aramco's Dhahran headquarters | 14 Oct
item.description:
A Houthi missile attack reportedly hit Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, and Riyadh struck back at Sanaa, taking the Saudi-Houthi war into the kingdom's oil heartland. In the Gulf, empty supertankers are steering away from a key transfer hub while Japanese buyers return to load crude by ship-to-ship transfer outside Hormuz.

item.title: Hormuz: 11 October count revised to six ships hit | 13 Oct
item.description:
A fuller count shows six merchant ships were hit around Hormuz on 11 October, and Gulf LNG flows remain far below pre-war levels as winter demand builds. Freight costs are also stranding heavy crude in the Americas, and Houthi strikes on Riyadh raise the risk of a wider war.
This episode is written with AI from public sources and read by an AI clone of Jaime's voice, not recorded by Jaime. Show notes link to every source.
In this episode: - Hormuz: 11 October count revised to six ships hit - Gulf LNG still down over 75%, Asia outbids Europe - Freight spike strands heavy crude in the Americas - Houthis strike Riyadh airport

item.title: Gulf: attacks spread beyond the Strait | 12 Oct

Early Monday the Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" had pulled prices lower, but the Middle East attacks outweighed it by the US session. European gas is at its highest since early 2023.
